title: Finding the Right Tone: Moving from Mechanics to Visuals
author: hwantasticgames
selftext:
I'm back again today.

A few days ago, I presented five different proposals, but instead of choosing any of them, I decided to proceed with the concept shown here. Frankly, if even this still feels like it has that "AI look," there isn't much more I can say, as I truly gave it a great deal of thought across numerous iterations.

Ultimately, I settled on a draft with a bright, cozy aesthetic. I had previously assumed it needed to be dark like a card table, but because this isn't a gambling game, adopting a far more casual tone felt like the right move.

Reflecting on the feedback, I realized this stemmed from a long-standing habit. I have been designing board games as a side project for about a decade. In board game design, artwork is secondary; if the core gameplay is solid and engaging, a publisher licenses the concept and produces a polished, visually appealing product. Accustomed to that dynamic, I rarely had to deliberate over visual assets.

The feedback gave me the opportunity to think much more deeply about art direction. I'm genuinely enjoying the process of evaluating drafts and making definitive decisions—it's exciting to truly feel like a director overseeing a comprehensive product. I will continue working to elevate the overall level of detail.

Thanks for your feedback again.
